sections.content: How many people are "paper and wood machine operatives"?

23,795 people

were counted on the census as "paper and wood machine operatives" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Paper and wood machine operatives operate machines to treat and cut wood, to produce, treat and cut paper, paperboard, leatherboard, plasterboard and similar material, and to assemble and make wooden crates and containers.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "paper and wood machine operatives" there were more men than women (87.6% compared with 12.4%).

This means "paper and wood machine operatives" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 87.6% and women made up 12.4% of "paper and wood machine operatives"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "paper and wood machine operatives" included:

  • production managers and directors in construction
  • roundspersons and van salespersons
  • air transport operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "paper and wood machine operatives" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "paper and wood machine operatives", 13.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "paper and wood machine operatives" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "paper and wood machine operatives" included:

  • plant and machine operatives (other)
  • refuse and salvage occupations
  • metal making and treating process operatives

We can look at who worked as "paper and wood machine operatives" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "paper and wood machine operatives" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "paper and wood machine operatives", 8.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (92% compared with 8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.3%) than self-employed (4.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Kingston upon Hull, City of, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
